title: Linear Combinations: Mix Two Arrows
topic: A linear combination is the recipe a·v1 + b·v2 with two scalar dials. Fix b at zero and sweep a — the output point glides along a line through the origin. Sweep both dials and the output paints out a region of the plane. Two non-parallel arrows reach every point in R^2 — that is what their span really means.

beats.narration: What can you build with just two arrows and a pair of dials?

elements.content: Two arrows. Two dials. How far does that get you?

beats.narration: Pick two arrows v one and v two. A linear combination is a v one plus b v two, where a and b are any two real numbers. That formula is the recipe.

v₂ vector in teal from origin
a and b are dials — any two real numbers

beats.narration: Fix b at zero and sweep the dial for a. The output point slides along a single line through the origin — the line of every multiple of v one.

elements.content: v₁ and v₂ stay drawn faintly
Output point P(t) = a(t)·v₁ slides through space as a sweeps from -2 → 2
Persistent trail painted along the v₁-line
a sweeps, b = 0 → P traces the line spanned by v₁

beats.narration: Now turn both dials at once. The point wanders all over the plane. Every reachable spot is some recipe a v one plus b v two — that whole region is the span.

elements.content: v₁ and v₂ in faint background
Output point P(a,b) = a·v₁ + b·v₂ wanders as (a,b) follow Lissajous curves over time
elements.note: drive (a,b) by useSprite localTime; show parallelogram of a·v₁ and b·v₂ as construction

elements.content: span(v₁, v₂) = { a·v₁ + b·v₂ : a, b ∈ ℝ }
Two non-parallel arrows fill the entire plane.

beats.narration: Linear combinations are how you turn arrows into reach. Two dials, two arrows, the whole plane.

elements.content: Two dials, two arrows — the whole plane.
(any reachable point has a unique recipe)
